svg.title: The supervisor-harness fence
svg.desc: Nested ceilings: the workspace, the run envelope, the task's scope and the agent's scope, each narrower than the last, over a floor no agent writes to: version control directories and the harness's own store.

text.tspan: Four ceilings, each narrower than the one above it. Authority only ever narrows, and every narrowing is recorded.
One run, one workspace root: every glob, the tool fence and the baseline commit are relative to it.
Granted once, before any task exists. The plan may narrow it; nothing widens it, not approval, not a task. It carries a date, and a stale
Proposed by the synthesis model and attenuated to the envelope. Editing it at approval clamps it the same way.
Attenuated at spawn to the envelope, to its task's scope and to its spawner's, so a verifier is never handed a wider fence than the
under all four, and not narrowed by anything above it
No agent writes to .git, .hg or .svn (a hook is code the tool runs) or to the harness's own store (the log every claim in the run is judged against), whatever its scope says,
A scope that exceeds its ceiling is narrowed to the intersection, not refused, and the ceiling that bit is recorded on the log.
